_doc: The declared partition of the quic-interop-runner matrix for this client.
It is the expected side of the comparison performed by assert_partition.py;
the observed side is the runner's own --json output. Every cell is asserted
in BOTH directions: a 'succeeded' row that comes back 'unsupported' is a
capability regression, and an 'unsupported' row that comes back 'succeeded'
means the exit-127 table in test/interop/quic/main.go now lies about us.
Either way the fix is a code change plus one edit here, never a retry.
'expect' is one result for every server, or an object keyed by server when
the partition genuinely differs - see rebind-port and connectionmigration,
where the outcome is decided by how strict the peer is.
An 'expect' of null - for a whole cell, or for one server inside the object
- declares the cell deliberately NOT asserted. It is still printed with
whatever it actually did, on every run, so it can never go unnoticed; it
just does not decide the verdict. That is the only tolerance in this file,
it costs a named cell and a stated reason, and today it is spent on exactly
two (cell, server) pairs whose outcome was measured to be probabilistic.
'testcase' is the TESTCASE string the runner hands the container, which is
NOT the matrix cell name: TestCase.testname() maps many cells onto one.
It is recorded so a row can be traced to its entry in main.go's support map.
Third-party images are pinned by digest. A tag would let someone else's
release move this gate with no commit of ours.
BASELINE. Every value below was observed on GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04
runners, in THREE independent full-matrix runs of this workflow (actions
runs 31852258646, 31853006121 and 31854123137). Nineteen of the twenty-two
cells were identical in all three runs against both servers.
The third run is the reason this file says what it says. After two runs the
three fault-injection cells looked stable on one server each, and this file
briefly asserted that. The third run contradicted it on both servers, so
n=2 was simply not enough to tell a stable cell from a coin flip. Anyone
tempted to tighten a not-asserted row back up should collect more samples
than that, and should note that all five not-asserted pairs are network
fault injection - none of them is a capability the client claims.

handshake.why: the base case: one connection, one file

longrtt.why: the handshake case again, with a long RTT

transfer.why: several streams in flight on one connection

multiplexing.why: enough streams to hit the peer's limit and resume on MAX_STREAMS

retry.why: the server forces a Retry; the token is echoed in a second Initial

http3.why: the only cell that uses ALPN h3 and the http3 package

blackhole.why: a transfer that survives the link going dark

amplificationlimit.why: a 9-certificate chain, so the server is held at the anti-amplification limit

ipv6.why: the same transfer over IPv6 only

rebind-port.why: the simulator rewrites the client's source port mid-transfer. Against quic-go the transfer completes; against ngtcp2 it stalls and the client gives up with 'read udp 193.167.0.100:...->193.167.100.100:443: i/o timeout'. Stable across both baseline runs on both servers, so this is a property of the pairing and not noise. The mechanism has not been diagnosed - the client does answer PATH_CHALLENGE (quic/conn_recv.go, OnPathChallenge) and does track peer connection IDs (quic/connid.go), so do not assume either is the cause; the pcaps are in the run's interop-logs-ngtcp2 artifact.

rebind-addr.why: the same as rebind-port, with the source address rewritten as well as the port. Deterministic against ngtcp2 - failed in all three baseline runs, the same i/o timeout - so that half is asserted. NOT ASSERTED against quic-go: it succeeded in the first two baseline runs and failed in the third, so the same stall this client has against ngtcp2 is reachable against quic-go too, just not every time.

connectionmigration.why: the cell reaches the CLIENT as a plain 'transfer', so the support table cannot decline it, and this client never performs an active migration. The two servers disagree about the cell rather than about us: quic-go's server exits 127 for TESTCASE=connectionmigration, which the runner reads as unsupported for the whole cell, while ngtcp2 serves it - the transfer then completes ('Check of downloaded files succeeded' in the log) and the runner still fails the cell, because no migration appears in the trace.

handshakeloss.why: NOT ASSERTED on either server: measured probabilistic. 50 sequential handshakes under 30% packet loss, each against the hard 10s per-connection cap (handshakeTimeout, quic/pto.go) - the first baseline failure logged 'connection 3/50: handshake: context deadline exceeded'. Over three baseline runs it went F/S/S against quic-go and S/S/F against ngtcp2. Asserting any value would make the tag gate red for a reason that is neither a regression nor a fix, and a gate that flakes gets switched off. Raise the cap or make it adaptive and this becomes assertable; until then the observed value is printed on every run.

handshakecorruption.why: NOT ASSERTED on either server, for exactly the reason handshakeloss is not: the same 50 connections against the same 10s cap, with 30% corruption instead of loss. S/F/F against quic-go and S/S/F against ngtcp2 over the three baseline runs. Note this does not match test/interop/quic/README.md, which records it as a deterministic failure; that measurement came from a WSL2 host whose clock stepped backwards mid-run, and the truth is that it is neither reliably pass nor reliably fail.

chacha20.why: the ClientHello must offer TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256 alone; crypto/tls ignores Config.CipherSuites for TLS 1.3

keyupdate.why: the client never initiates a key update - it stops at the AEAD confidentiality limit and closes (quic/conn_seal.go)

resumption.why: session resumption is an explicit non-goal: no session cache is installed (quic/handshake.go)

zerortt.why: 0-RTT is an explicit non-goal, for the same reason resumption is (quic/handshake.go)

ecn.why: outgoing packets are not ECN-marked and ACK_ECN counts are parsed but discarded (quic/frame.go)

v2.why: QUIC v1 only: the version_information transport parameter is not sent, so compatible version negotiation never starts

versionnegotiation.why: NOT ASSERTED because it never runs: it is declared in main.go's support table, but TestCaseVersionNegotiation is absent from the pinned runner's TESTCASES_QUIC list, so the matrix does not ask for it. Kept here so the declared set stays the set main.go declares.
